records.text: On 2023-05-25, the user asked for Midjourney documentation to be organized into tables. The user first requested a table for the preceding content, which covered aspect ratios and the chaos parameter; the assistant instead supplied a table summarizing the quality parameter. The user then provided material about Midjourney seeds and requested a table, and the assistant organized it by concept, description, examples, finding a job’s seed, and changing seed numbers.

Midjourney’s --seed accepts whole numbers from 0 to 4,294,967,295 and influences the initial image grid. Without a specified seed, Midjourney generates one randomly. The same prompt, seed, and parameters produce identical images in Model Versions 4 and niji; Versions 1, 2, 3, test, and testp are non-deterministic and produce similar but not identical images.

Midjourney’s --sameseed accepts whole numbers from 0 to 4,294,967,295, creates a shared large noise field for all images in an initial grid, and is compatible with Model Versions 1, 2, 3, test, and testp. It tends to make the generated images very similar.

A Midjourney job’s seed can be found by reacting to the job with an envelope emoji in Discord. To retrieve a past job, use /show with its job ID to revive it, then react to the revived job with an envelope emoji. Seed parameters can be added to the end of a prompt as --seed <value> or --sameseed <value>.
